captions.detailed: This 3D model is a flexible, segmented circular bracelet designed for 3D printing. It consists of concentric inner and outer thin-walled rings that are connected by a pattern of zig-zagging internal flexible struts (spikes) forming triangular voids. The outer ring features vertical slit gaps at regular intervals to allow expansion, and a customized text string is embossed or debossed directly onto the outer segments.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric, flexible segmented bracelet in OpenSCAD with adjustable inner and outer radii, height, and number of segments. The design must feature concentric inner and outer rings connected by internal flexible spikes with regular expansion gaps, and support customizable text wrapped around the outer perimeter.
captions.factory: The script constructs the bracelet by combining an inner ring and an outer ring, both created using the difference of two cylinders. These rings are split into sections by subtracting arrays of cubes (innerholes and outerholes) rotated around the center. A series of connecting internal diagonal struts are generated using linear_extrude of custom polygons in a loop. Finally, custom text is mapped onto the outer cylinder's surface by scaling and rotating extruded 2D polygons from a font library, which is then subtracted from the main body depending on the selected part mode.
